Bulk RNA-seq differential expression

Example report: dexamethasone response in human airway smooth muscle cells

Published

November 13, 2026

Note

This is a portfolio example built on public data. It shows the structure, depth and turnaround-ready format of a standard bulk RNA-seq deliverable. Client reports follow the same layout, with the study’s own design, contrasts and questions.

Summary

Show code 
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(airway); library(DESeq2); library(apeglm); library(ggplot2); library(ggrepel)
  library(pheatmap); library(fgsea); library(msigdbr); library(AnnotationDbi); library(org.Hs.eg.db)
  library(dplyr); library(knitr)
})
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "", ifelse(p < 1e-300, "< 1e-300", formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 1)))
fmt_fc <- function(l) ifelse(l >= 0, sprintf("%.1f\u00d7 up", 2^l), sprintf("%.1f\u00d7 down", 2^-l))
data(airway)
se <- airway
se$dex <- relevel(factor(se$dex), ref = "untrt")
se$cell <- factor(se$cell)
dds <- DESeqDataSet(se, design = ~ cell + dex)
keep <- rowSums(counts(dds) >= 10) >= 3
dds <- dds[keep, ]
dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds, name = "dex_trt_vs_untrt", alpha = 0.05)
res_s <- lfcShrink(dds, coef = "dex_trt_vs_untrt", type = "apeglm", res = res)
sym <- mapIds(org.Hs.eg.db, keys = rownames(res_s), keytype = "ENSEMBL", column = "SYMBOL", multiVals = "first")
tab <- as.data.frame(res_s) |> mutate(gene_id = rownames(res_s), symbol = ifelse(is.na(sym), gene_id, sym)) |> arrange(padj)
sig <- tab |> filter(!is.na(padj), padj < 0.05)
up <- sum(sig$log2FoldChange > 1); down <- sum(sig$log2FoldChange < -1)
  • Design: four primary airway smooth muscle cell lines, each treated with 1 µM dexamethasone for 18 hours or left untreated (8 samples, paired by donor). Data: Himes et al., PLoS ONE 2014 (GEO GSE52778), via the Bioconductor airway package.
  • Genes tested: 16,596 genes with at least 10 reads in at least 3 samples.
  • Result: 4,099 genes changed at a false discovery rate below 5%; 431 rose and 376 fell by more than two-fold.
  • Biology check: the strongest responses include classic glucocorticoid-induced genes (shown below), which confirms the treatment worked and the analysis is oriented correctly.
  • Quality: samples separate first by treatment and second by donor, with no outlier samples.

Quality control

Show code 
ls <- data.frame(sample = colnames(dds), reads = colSums(counts(dds)) / 1e6, dex = dds$dex, cell = dds$cell)
ggplot(ls, aes(reorder(sample, reads), reads, fill = dex)) + geom_col(width = 0.7) + coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(untrt = "#8a94a6", trt = "#1f6f8b"), labels = c("Untreated", "Dexamethasone")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Assigned reads (millions)", fill = NULL, title = "Library sizes")

Library sizes range from 15.1 to 30.8 million reads, all adequate for gene-level analysis. Differences are absorbed by DESeq2’s size factors.

Show code 
vsd <- vst(dds, blind = TRUE)
pc <- plotPCA(vsd, intgroup = c("dex", "cell"), returnData = TRUE)
pv <- round(100 * attr(pc, "percentVar"))
ggplot(pc, aes(PC1, PC2, color = dex, shape = cell)) + geom_point(size = 4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(untrt = "#8a94a6", trt = "#1f6f8b"), labels = c("Untreated", "Dexamethasone")) +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 (", pv[1], "% of variance)"), y = paste0("PC2 (", pv[2], "% of variance)"), color = "Treatment", shape = "Donor line",
       title = "Principal components (variance-stabilized counts)")

Treatment drives the first component and donor the second, which is why the model includes donor as a blocking factor (a paired design).

Show code 
d <- as.matrix(dist(t(assay(vsd))))
ann <- data.frame(Treatment = ifelse(vsd$dex == "trt", "Dexamethasone", "Untreated"), Donor = as.character(vsd$cell), row.names = colnames(vsd))
pheatmap(d, annotation_col = ann, annotation_row = ann, show_colnames = FALSE, main = "Sample-to-sample distances",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("#1f3b57", "#f4f6f8"))(50),
         annotation_colors = list(Treatment = c(Dexamethasone = "#1f6f8b", Untreated = "#8a94a6")))

Differential expression

Show code 
tab$class <- with(tab, ifelse(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange > 1, "Up",
                       ifelse(!is.na(padj) & padj < 0.05 & log2FoldChange < -1, "Down", "Not significant")))
lab <- tab |> filter(class != "Not significant") |> slice_min(padj, n = 18)
ggplot(tab |> filter(!is.na(padj)), aes(log2FoldChange, -log10(padj), color = class)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(label = symbol), size = 3, color = "black", max.overlaps = 30) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Up = "#c0392b", Down = "#1f6f8b", `Not significant` = "#c9ced6")) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  labs(x = "log2 fold change (dexamethasone vs untreated, shrunken)", y = "-log10 adjusted p", color = NULL, title = "Volcano plot")
Show code 
ggplot(tab |> filter(baseMean > 0), aes(log10(baseMean), log2FoldChange, color = class)) + geom_point(size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Up = "#c0392b", Down = "#1f6f8b", `Not significant` = "#c9ced6")) +
  labs(x = "log10 mean normalized count", y = "log2 fold change", color = NULL, title = "MA plot")

Known glucocorticoid-response genes

These genes are textbook targets of the glucocorticoid receptor; CRISPLD2 was the gene highlighted in the original study. Seeing them near the top of the list is the main sanity check that the contrast is the right way round.

Show code 
top <- tab |> filter(!is.na(padj)) |> slice_min(padj, n = 40)
m <- assay(vst(dds))[top$gene_id, ]
m <- m - rowMeans(m); rownames(m) <- top$symbol
pheatmap(m, annotation_col = ann, show_colnames = FALSE, fontsize_row = 7, main = "Top 40 genes (row-centred expression)",
         color = colorRampPalette(c("#1f6f8b", "#f7f7f7", "#c0392b"))(60), border_color = NA,

Pathways

Show code 
h <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H")
sets <- split(h$ensembl_gene, h$gs_name)
st <- res$stat; names(st) <- rownames(res); st <- sort(st[!is.na(st)], decreasing = TRUE)
set.seed(1)
gs <- fgsea(sets, st, minSize = 15, maxSize = 500)
gs <- gs |> arrange(padj)
showp <- gs |> filter(padj < 0.05) |> slice_max(abs(NES), n = 16) |> mutate(pathway = gsub("HALLMARK_", "", pathway) |> gsub(pattern = "_", replacement = " "))
ggplot(showp, aes(NES, reorder(pathway, NES), fill = NES > 0)) + geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#c0392b", `FALSE` = "#1f6f8b"), labels = c(`TRUE` = "Higher with dexamethasone", `FALSE` = "Lower with dexamethasone")) +
  labs(x = "Normalized enrichment score", y = NULL, fill = NULL, title = "Hallmark gene sets (FDR < 5%)") + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Gene set enrichment on the full ranked list (no cut-off) found 18 of the 50 Hallmark sets changed at FDR below 5%.

Methods (ready to paste into a manuscript)

Gene-level read counts for eight samples (four donor airway smooth muscle cell lines, each untreated or treated with 1 µM dexamethasone for 18 h; GEO GSE52778) were obtained from the Bioconductor airway package. Genes with at least 10 counts in at least three samples were retained (16,596 genes). Differential expression was tested with DESeq2 (v1.52.0) using a paired design (~ donor + treatment); log2 fold changes were shrunk with apeglm, and p-values were adjusted with the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. Genes with adjusted p < 0.05 were considered significant. Gene set enrichment analysis against the MSigDB Hallmark collection was performed with fgsea (v1.38.0) on genes ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic. Analyses were run in R 4.6.2.

Deliverables in a client project

  • This report (HTML and PDF), with all figures as separate high-resolution PNG and vector PDF files
  • Full results table for every gene (Excel and CSV): counts, fold changes, p-values, gene annotations
  • Normalized expression matrix and the analysis code, so results can be reproduced
  • A 30-minute call to walk through the findings
